# Nav Gurm's Vision for Fresno.
Addressing Cost of Living
Fresno families, like mine and yours, are feeling the pinch of rising costs—from inflation and gas prices to housing and utilities. I will fight to ensure that our local utility rates remain affordable and that every city service is cost-effective for our residents.
Strengthening Public Safety
A safe Fresno is a thriving Fresno. I will work to ensure that our police and fire departments have the resources and personnel they need to protect and serve our neighborhoods.
Investing in Fresno’s Economy
To build a stronger economy, we need to support the backbone of our city—small businesses—while fostering innovation and recruiting major employers offering career-track jobs
Parks
Our parks are vital spaces for families, children, and seniors alike. I will launch an annual survey to ensure our parks are clean, accessible, and meeting the needs of every resident.
Fair Share of Dollars
Fresno deserves its fair share of state and federal funding. I will work tirelessly to bring those dollars home.
Homelessness
Homelessness requires a compassionate yet practical approach. I will foster partnerships between the city, county, nonprofits, and faith-based organizations to deliver real solutions.
Infrastructure
Fresno’s roads, sidewalks, and infrastructure need serious attention. I will prioritize fixing potholes, modernizing our transit systems, and ensuring that every neighborhood has access to safe and reliable infrastructure.
Sports and Entertainment
Sports and entertainment bring communities together and put cities on the map. I’ll work to bring professional soccer to Fresno, support Fresno State’s entry into the PAC-12, and advocate for expanding entertainment venues across the city. Sports can be a catalyst for economic growth and civic pride.
A Vision for Blackstone and Manchester Mall
Manchester Mall has the potential to become Fresno’s first major mixed-use development—a vibrant space where people can live, work, shop, and play. I will work with developers, investors, and community members to turn this vision into reality, making Blackstone a corridor of opportunity for all.
Housing
Fresno must address its housing crisis by increasing the supply of all types of housing—affordable units, starter homes, and market-rate apartments. I will streamline approval processes and work with builders to ensure we meet the needs of a growing population without sacrificing quality or sustainability.
Engaging the Youth
Our city’s future depends on our young people. I will create initiatives to engage youth in decision-making processes, expand mentorship and internship opportunities, and support programs that inspire the next generation of Fresno leaders. Investing in our youth is investing in Fresno’s success.
Seniors and Veterans
Our seniors and veterans have given so much to our community, and it’s time we give back. I will advocate for expanded senior services, improved healthcare access, and programs that honor and support our veterans. Ensuring dignity and opportunity for these groups is a personal priority for me.
Constituent Services
Every resident deserves to have their voice heard. I will establish accessible office hours, improve communication channels, and ensure that every concern—big or small—is addressed promptly. My commitment is to serve as an advocate for every person in District 7 – you deserve a response from your Councilmember.
Fiscal Responsibility
Fresno’s budget must reflect the priorities of its residents. I will ensure that every dollar spent delivers tangible results, cutting waste and increasing transparency. Fiscal responsibility isn’t just about balancing the budget—it’s about investing in our community’s future.

# ON THE ISSUES
# ROB'S PRIORITIES
#### Affordability
Our living expenses are skyrocketing, as costs continue to rise for gas, groceries, and other essentials. Rob will be laser-focused on promoting policies and programs that reduce or assist with the costs of housing, utilities, transportation, and childcare. He will call for public hearings and public input regarding the rates of city services, and he will fight to drive down the costs and expand the availability of multi-family and single-family housing throughout our city.
#### Public Safety
Fresno families deserve to feel safe in their homes. Rob will partner with law enforcement, mental health professionals, and community leaders to build safer, stronger neighborhoods by combining measures that increase accountability while focusing on prevention. He will launch a “Clean Up District 1” initiative, working with law and code enforcement to target crime hotspots and crack down on illegal dumping and nuisance properties.
#### Homelessness
The government has spent billions of dollars on homelessness, but we’ve made very little progress in addressing the homelessness crisis. Rob advocates for supportive housing with wraparound services (including mental health and substance abuse treatment) for the chronically homeless, and rapid rehousing for the newly homeless. However, he will call for a study of comparable cities to determine what works, and what doesn't work, before we spend more taxpayer money. He’ll also aggressively expand access to affordable housing to prevent new incidence of homelessness.
#### Jobs & Economic Growth
Rob has dedicated his career to expanding opportunities for Fresno’s working families. A committed coalition builder, Rob will work with our business and labor communities to spur economic development, attracting and retaining businesses, creating good-paying jobs, and expanding opportunities for every person who calls Fresno home. He’ll work to cut red tape that makes it unduly burdensome to build housing or to start a business in our otherwise vibrant neighborhoods.
#### Community Development
Our communities’ infrastructure is in desperate need of repair. Many neighborhoods in District 1 have not seen their streets or sidewalks fixed or repaved in literally decades. Rob’s priority will be squarely on revitalizing our existing neighborhoods, including by improving our street lighting; repairing our roads, sidewalks, and gutters; and expanding our parks, trees, and green spaces. Rob will work hand in hand with community partners to develop neighborhoods where residents can live, work, play, and thrive—neighborhoods that we are all proud to call home.

# About Lionel Lopez, Jr.
I was raised in Parlier. I shopped at Jepsen's and at Nico's, and I rode my bike over the dirt mounds where PAC Auto stands today. Like a lot of people my age, I left for a while — for school, and then for construction work out of state — and like fewer of them, I came back, because this is where I wanted to raise my family and build my business.
​
This community has given so much to me, and I am ready to give back.
​
I did not decide to run for Mayor on a whim. In November of 2025 I stood with a group of organized, respectful neighbors who brought a serious concern to the City Council, and I did not appreciate how we were dismissed. That moment drove me to take action. I have attended every single Council meeting since except two, I have read the agendas and the check registers, and I have gone to the podium on the water bills, on the cost of our pending lawsuits, and on the things residents were told would be handled and were not.
​
Running a construction business teaches you something that carries straight into City Hall: people can tell the difference between a job done right and a job done fast, and your name is on it either way. It also teaches you that when you make a promise about a timeline or a cost, someone is planning their life around your answer.
​
I believe leadership is a responsibility that should not be taken lightly, and that a leader has to hold himself accountable to the people who put him there, regardless of the consequences. I believe a city is less likely to be led astray when more people can see first-hand how everything is working. And I believe respect and trust are earned again every year — they last only so long as a leader continues to measure up to the demands of the office.
​
After much prayer and reflection, and with the unwavering support of my family and friends, I am running for Mayor of the beautiful City of Parlier. Parlier is not a stepping stone to something else. It is my home and it is my priority.
​
Restoring Our Roots, Growing Into The Future.
​
Paid for by Lopez For Mayor City of Parlier 2026, FPPC #1489459
​
​
## My Story
My Story — From Home in Parlier to Montana to N. Dakota to Houston to Home in Parlier
People ask me why I'm running for Mayor. The answer is in these three photos.
The first photo is me on a jobsite up in Montana and North Dakota, where I worked through brutal winters far from home. I've shown up in the coldest, hardest conditions and gotten the job done — and that's the same work ethic I'll bring to City Hall. No shortcuts. No excuses. Just showing up for the people who are counting on me.
​
The second photo, that's me standing next to the Space Shuttle in Houston where I lived for two years. Standing there, looking at something built by people who dared to dream big, I was reminded of a simple truth: with vision and hard work, there's almost nothing we can't accomplish. That belief never left me — and it's the same belief I have for Parlier. Our best days aren't behind us. They're ahead. But dreams don't build themselves.
​
And that last photo? That's the reason for all of it — my wife and our baby. Everything I've seen and everywhere I've been led me right back here, to Parlier. This is home. This is where we're raising our family, and this is the community I'm committed to serving.
I've dreamed big in Houston. I've worked hard across this country. Now I'm bringing all of it home — because Parlier deserves a mayor with vision AND the work ethic to make it real.
​
Let's get to work, Parlier. 🌱
​
🗳️ VOTE Lionel López for Mayor — Nov. 3rd
🌐 LopezForParlier2026.com
Restoring Our Roots, Growing Into the Future

## Yazmine Enriquez
Candidate for Mayor of Kerman, California
Fresh Ideas. Strong Roots. One Kerman.
# Rooted in Kerman
#### “Kerman is home because my family, my business, my memories, and my community are all here.”
For Yazmine Enriquez, Kerman isn't simply where she lives. It's where she grew up, where her family built a business, where she formed lifelong relationships, and where she chose to build her future.
Yazmine moved to Kerman at age 11 and grew up on a dairy just outside of town. Her memories of Kerman are filled with the everyday places and people that made the community feel like home: hot chocolate from Star 7 before school, donuts from Sunshine Donuts, evenings at Lions Park, the Harvest Festival, local restaurants, school activities, church at St. Patrick's, and the teachers and neighbors who helped shape her life.
As Kerman has grown, Yazmine believes one thing has remained constant: the heart of the community.
Read Yazmine's Story
Read Yazmine's Story
## About Yazmine
Yazmine's story begins long before her decision to run for office.
Growing up, she worked alongside her father on the family dairy, helping round up cattle and learning early that hard work requires communication, responsibility, and a willingness to get your hands dirty.
She later spent nine years with GUESS, advancing from Sales Associate to Assistant Manager and Interim Store Manager and serving as a Brand Ambassador. Her responsibilities included sales, hiring, training, customer service, personnel management, visual merchandising, operations, event execution, and developing and retaining employees.
In 2021, Yazmine left GUESS and returned home to help operate her family's business, Fruta Fresca.
That decision ultimately brought her closer to the community she had grown up in.
## A Small-Business Owner Who Understands What It Takes
Fruta Fresca opened in Kerman on June 6, 2012, just two days after Yazmine graduated from high school.
What began as a family ice cream business has grown into a place where generations of families visit, community events take shape, new flavors are created, and relationships are built.
Today, Yazmine helps manage the business alongside her parents. Her responsibilities include payroll, scheduling, paperwork, staffing, ingredient sourcing, inventory, production coordination, community outreach, events, and the unexpected problems that come with operating a small business.
It has given her firsthand experience with the opportunities and challenges facing local businesses.
# Community Means Showing Up
Yazmine's community involvement grew naturally through Fruta Fresca.
One introduction led to an event. One event led to another connection. Those connections led to school-supply drives, family scavenger hunts, community partnerships, volunteer work, Rotary activities, public-safety events, and countless smaller opportunities to help.
Her first major community event after returning to Kerman was National Night Out with the Kerman Police Department. Yazmine credits Officer Cubillos with introducing her to the event and opening the door to deeper community involvement.
### “To me, community is the people who make a place feel like home.”
Read Yazmine's Story
## Focused on Kerman's Future
Yazmine's experiences as a resident, small-business owner, volunteer, and community organizer have shaped the issues she believes deserve attention.
### Supporting Local Business
Clearer processes, better communication, reasonable permitting timelines, opportunities for local businesses to participate in community events, and a meaningful voice for small-business owners.
### Responsible Growth
Kerman is growing. Yazmine believes growth should create opportunities while preserving the hometown character and community connections longtime residents value.
### Youth & Families
More opportunities for young people and families to connect, participate, develop interests, and envision a future in Kerman.
### Community Engagement
Local government works best when residents can be heard and understand what is happening in their community.
# One Kerman
Kerman has changed since Yazmine first arrived at age 11. It has grown, welcomed new families and businesses, and created new opportunities.
But its strength continues to come from its people.
Yazmine wants to help Kerman move forward without losing the relationships, pride, history, and hometown character that make it home.
